about: The postcommunio of the formulary “Commemoration of All the Faithful Departed — Mass III” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Grant, we beseech You, O almighty and merciful God, that the souls of Your servants and handmaids for whom we have offered this sacrifice of praise to Your Majesty, cleansed of all sins by the power of this sacrament, may, by Your mercy, receive the joy of perpetual light. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who lives and reigns with You in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, forever and ever.

a.g: we have offered to Thy Majesty

nt.w019: Tuæ can mean either “Your” with “Majesty” or “Your” with “praise.” Here it is joined to “Majesty,” the recipient of the offering. The Latin contains only one possessive, so it is not repeated in both phrases.
